newsitem.title: USA: African officials in US meet Rubin, discuss reform.
newsitem.headline: African officials in US meet Rubin, discuss reform.

text.p: Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin on Monday met officials from eight African countries, including some who may qualify for a new debt-relief initiative, to discuss the continent's economic reforms.

A senior Treasury official, speaking to reporters later, said the two-hour session was largely to talk about the African nations' approaches to such issues as permitting a greater private-sector role in their economies and to building stronger financial systems.
Finance ministers and central governors from Botswana, Ethiopia, Ghana, Kenya, Mauritius, Mozambique, Senegal and Uganda and from the central bank of West African States attended.

Uganda has been mentioned as a top contender for a proposal endorsed by the joint Development Committee of the World Bank and International Monetary Fund that aims to lift the burden on countries forced to spend the benefits of economic growth servicing their debts.
The initiative, involving action by creditor countries, the IMF and the World Bank, will cost up to $7.7 billion.

The African finance officials stressed their interest in getting greater access to U.S. markets for products like textiles. They also said they wanted U.S. firms to learn more about trade and investment opportunities in Africa, the Treasury official said.

The African representatives urged the United States to soon make up its late payments to the International Development Association, a position that Rubin has regularly endorsed in appearances before Congress.
